Oliver Goldsmith, The Vicar of Wakefield.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/oliver-goldsmith/the-vicar-of-wakefield

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Oliver Goldsmith, the author and the writer of a preface, died 1774 (Wikidata Q236236, P570 = 1774-04-04; Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Goldsmith).

First publication of the text used: 'The Vicar of Wakefield was published in 1766 by Oliver Goldsmith.' (SE colophon).

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1766, before 1929. Works published before 1929 entered the United States public domain by 1 January 2025, and Standard Ebooks states the same in its rights statement (below).
- Country of origin: every person whose words are in the text died in 1774 or earlier; the last to die was Oliver Goldsmith in 1774 (Wikidata Q236236, P570 = 1774-04-04). So the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less, whatever its country of first publication.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
